issue.issue_text: Whether the continued incarceration of the appellant was justified.

facts: The appellant, a Chartered Accountant, had been in jail since September 26, 2022, in connection with a money-laundering case.
The money-laundering case (ECIR) was a sequel to an FIR for a predicate offence that was filed nine years earlier, in 2013.
No final report or charge-sheet had been filed in the underlying predicate offence case for the past nine years.
The original complainant in the 2013 FIR was later arrested as an accused by the Enforcement Directorate in the money-laundering case, but the court rejected the ED's application for his remand.
law: The Court considered the conditions for granting bail under Section 45 of the Prevention of Money-laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA).

Specifically, the Court assessed whether the second condition under Section 45(1)(ii) was met, which requires the court to have reasonable grounds to believe that the accused is not guilty of the offence.
application: The Court found that the long delay and lack of progress in the nine-year-old predicate offence case weakened the foundation of the money-laundering charges against the appellant.
The fact that the original complainant was now being treated as an accused, and his remand was rejected, gave the court further reason to doubt the prosecution's case.

Based on these circumstances, the Court determined there was a valid argument that the second condition for bail under Section 45 of the PMLA was satisfied, meaning there were reasonable grounds to believe the appellant was not guilty.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the continued incarceration of the appellant was not justified and ordered him to be released on bail.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the continued incarceration of the appellant was justified.
appellant_arguments: The appellant, a Chartered Accountant by profession, has been in jail since September 26, 2022, and their continued incarceration is not justified.
respondent_arguments: The continued incarceration of the appellant is justified based on the stringent conditions for bail under Section 45 of the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act (PMLA).
